plain: To lessen or die down, as a storm, pain, or anger does

webster.text: To beat down; to pull down; to destroy in any manner; as to abate a nuisance.

more.text: To lessen; to diminish; to moderate; as to abate zeal; to abate pride; to abate a demand; to abate courage.
To lessen; to mitigate; as to abate pain or sorrow.
To cause to fail; to annul.
To decrease, or become less in strength or violence; as pain abates; a storm abates.

example.quote: He had thought it necessary, for this & other reasons that the plan should have been proposed in a more mediating shape, in order to abate the heat and opposition of parties.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, September 17, 1787
